transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I’m here because ever since my in-laws moved into our house, I’ve just been incredibly keyed up and, honestly, completely worn down. 

It's bleeding into everything. I’m snapping at my wife all the time. And work has been a mess. I'm an agent, and lately I've found myself avoiding calls that I would normally handle immediately. It actually got to the point where I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart the other day just because I couldn’t think straight. So, I figured I needed to come in and get a handle on this.
Did these feelings start after your in-laws moved into your house?

Yeah, exactly. I was functioning completely normally before they moved in. Everything at work and at home was fine. But then they arrived, and... I'd say within just a few weeks of them basically taking over the house, all of this started.
Since this started, have you been feeling down or depressed?

No, I wouldn't really say I feel depressed. It's not a sadness, if that makes sense. It's more just... I'm constantly on edge and completely stressed out. I just feel overwhelmed by the whole situation at the house, but I don't feel down in that way.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different parts of your life, not just the situation with your in-laws?

No, not really. It's... it's pretty much all tied to the situation at the house. I mean, I guess I'm worried about work right now, but only because my focus is so shot from dealing with my in-laws that I'm dropping the ball. 

I don't just sit around worrying about random things or other parts of my life. Before they moved in, I wasn't an anxious person at all. It all really just comes back to them being in our space and how much it's disrupting everything.
Since this started, have you been losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I still like doing the things I normally enjoy. It's just... well, it's harder to actually find the peace and quiet to do them right now with a full house. But the interest is definitely still there. I haven't lost that.
